thesis: The bull carried the debate narrowly because Meta's exceptional margins, free cash flow, leverage, and forward P/E discount provide a stronger base than the price action suggests. The ruling remains low confidence: AI-capex returns, settlement costs, and missing technical structure make this a monitoring bias rather than a precise trade instruction.
strongest_counterexample: If AI spending fails to create incremental revenue while settlement payments and restrictions reduce platform economics, the 16.96x forward P/E can represent deteriorating earnings rather than undervaluation.
invalidation_conditions: Operating margin falls below 35% for two consecutive reported quarters.
Trailing FCF falls below $35B for two consecutive Layer 1 refreshes.
AI investment is followed by two quarters of revenue growth below 10% without margin improvement.
Settlement costs or restrictions cause a material downward revision to earnings expectations.
evidence_gaps: SMA/RSI/Bollinger/ATR/support/resistance are unavailable after the non-finite 2026-08-28 bar.
Layer 1 has no incremental AI-revenue bridge or capex-return schedule.
Exact settlement payment conditions and operating impact require primary-company confirmation.
decisive_factors: Available EMA/MACD rebound evidence tempered by incomplete technical coverage.
